questions.question: A helmet should not:

options.text: Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: A good helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no obvious defects. If a helmet was worn during a crash, replace it.

questions.question: A motorcyclist can discourage other vehicles from lane sharing by:

options.text: Riding in the left portion of a lane.
Riding in the center portion of a lane.
Giving dirty looks if another driver moves into their lane.
Riding in a zigzag pattern to fill up a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in the center portion of a lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to prevent other drivers from squeezing into your space.

questions.question: The middle of the lane usually has an oily strip. You should:

options.text: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
Ride only on the oily strip because it provides better grip.
Avoid the entire center portion of the lane.
Not worry about oil or debris in a lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid the oily strip when it is raining.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars builds up in the middle of each lane. On dry roads, this strip usually has enough grip for a motorcycle. When wet, avoid it. The strip is narrow enough that you can ride around it while staying in the center portion of the lane.

questions.question: If you brake while turning:

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You will have more grip as you lean into the turn.
You may have less grip as you lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the turn.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. When leaning into a turn, some of your tire's grip is used for turning. Less grip is left for braking.

questions.question: Of crashes between a motorcycle and a car, how many are caused by the car driver failing to yield the right-of-way?
questions.correctAnswerText: Over 50 percent
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle-car crashes happen because the car driver did not yield the right-of-way to the motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding in a group, inexperienced riders should ride:

options.text: In the front of the group.
At the back of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This way, they won't fall behind, and experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in one lane position and never move.
Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Only ride in the center of the lane so other vehicles see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Move your position as road and traffic conditions change.

questions.question: If the throttle is stuck, you should:

options.text: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
Not try to twist the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Twist the throttle back and forth several times.
questions.explanation: If the throttle is stuck, twist it back and forth several times to free it. If that does not work, use the engine cut-off switch and pull in the clutch at the same time.

questions.question: Which portion of the lane should always be avoided?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane
No portion should always be avoided.

questions.correctAnswerText: No portion should always be avoided.
questions.explanation: No lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Choose a lane position based on current riding conditions.

questions.question: When riding with a passenger, you should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid talking to the passenger while riding.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so your motorcycle responds more slowly. Ride slower than normal, slow down sooner, and increase your following distance. Always talk to your passenger to warn them of any road conditions ahead.

questions.question: When riding through a curve, a group of motorcyclists should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a single-file formation.
questions.explanation: Riders should switch to single-file formation when going through curves, making turns, entering a highway, or leaving a highway. This is safer than a staggered formation.

questions.question: Face shields and goggles:

options.text: Will likely never need to be replaced.
Will develop scratches and become brittle, requiring regular replacement.
Should be made of breakable materials so they break away in a crash.
Should not allow air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will develop scratches and become brittle, requiring regular replacement.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. Over time, they will get scratched and become brittle. Replace them regularly to stay safe and comfortable.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Place inexperienced riders at the back of the group.
Not tailgate other riders within the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not tailgate other riders within the group.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when group riding. Check your mirrors often to watch other riders. The lead and sweep riders should be experienced. Keep proper spacing between all riders in the group.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road hazards or conditions.

questions.question: When both braking and swerving must be done to avoid a hazard, a rider should:

options.text: Perform one action, then the other.
Perform both actions at the same time and apply extra braking pressure.
Perform both actions at the same time, but mainly focus on swerving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Perform one action, then the other.
questions.explanation: Do not brake and swerve at the same time. You need good traction to swerve safely. Do one action first, then the other.

questions.question: Each traffic lane gives the motorcyclist how many paths of travel?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane has three paths for motorcyclists: left, center, and right.

questions.question: When loading cargo onto a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
Pack lighter items near the front.
Try to not place items over the rear axle.
Place items behind the rear axle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pack heavier items in front of the tank bag.
questions.explanation: Load heavier items in front of the tank bag. Place the load over or in front of the rear axle. Putting the load behind the rear axle will make it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.question: Without a helmet, a motorcycle rider is ________ more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.
questions.correctAnswerText: Five times
questions.explanation: Without a helmet, riders are five times more likely to suffer a critical head injury in a crash.

questions.question: To increase your chances of being seen at an intersection, you should:

options.text: Try to make eye contact with other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride with your headlight on.
questions.explanation: Ride with your headlight on and position your motorcycle so oncoming traffic can see you easily. Keep a safe distance from other vehicles. Never assume a driver sees you, even if you make eye contact.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the roadway, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an obstacle, try to hit it at a 90-degree angle. Slow down as much as you can before impact. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off your seat, and roll the throttle slightly to lighten the front end just before hitting it.
